messages.subject: Area coverted to 1
parts:
A quick question about Area.

When the area is UNKNOWN and you are converting area to 1 in your analysis,
does your Density Estimate represent 1 unit of measure (eg: meter or
meter sq.) or 1 transect?

Thanks,

Pam

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Area coverted to 1
parts:
On Mon, 11 Jan 1999 18:52:35 -0500 (EST), Pamela McRae wrote:

> >
> >A quick question about Area.
> >
> > When the area is UNKNOWN and you are converting area to 1 in your analysis,
> >does your Density Estimate represent 1 unit of measure (eg: meter or
> > meter sq.) or 1 transect?

Density (D) is always abundance per unit area, whether the area is known or
not. You will have defined the units of area (e.g., meter sq.) when you set up
the project.

(It is the abundance (N) estimate that is affected by the area that you have
entered in the stratum data layer - if you don't enter anything the default is
1 unit area per stratum. If you only have one stratum, then total area will be
1 and the density and abundance estimates will be the same (except that
abunance is rounded to the nearest whole number). Generally though, if your
area is unknown then ignore the abundance estimates.)

Hope this helps,

- Len
